purpose: Master of Game/Music/ember-punk-04.wav, which the game plays since #443: written from this file by Tools/MusicBake --tracks (brought to the loudness of the procedural piece in its slot, peaks held under full scale, 16-bit PCM).
provenance: Generated first for home listening under the name ember-green-day-0N: at the owner's request this prompt NAMES a real band and a real song/album as the style reference (the punk-01..03 prompts only described the style). The owner listened and judged, 2026-09-16: neither recording is recognisable as Green Day or as a specific song; cleared to rename and use in the game.
generator: ACE-Step 1.5 (acestep.cpp v0.0.5), local, AMD RX 6900 XT via Vulkan -- generate-music.ps1 -NoCotCaption -Loop
format: 48000 Hz, 32-bit float PCM, stereo -- 48 kHz is the model's fixed native rate
lm_enriched_caption: none -- use_cot_caption was false, so the LM passed the caption through verbatim and only filled bpm, key and duration

request.caption: Green Day style punk rock instrumental, like Green Day's Boulevard of Broken Dreams: brooding mid-tempo, tremolo-picked distorted guitar melody, palm-muted power chords in the verses opening into big anthemic choruses, steady marching snare, melancholic and defiant, no vocals
request.lm_negative_prompt: vocals, singing, audience applause, crowd noise, live recording

post_process: loop_crossfade.py: a 16-bar loop cut out of the render's body -- source 37.22s..82.40s, tempo measured 84.8 bpm, 1.41s equal-power crossfade -> 45.2s seamless loop
loop_check: crossfade rhythm r=0.86 against the track's own passages a bar apart r=0.50; spectrum cos=0.79; context match 0.608 (best 0.657). Verdict: in time
